findings.title: Stop requiring a user before showing conditional passkeys, which breaks normal passkey login
Ensure the passkey used during re-authentication belongs to the already-identified user
Avoid util-to-browser package dependency by moving the constant
Use `assertThrows` instead of try/fail/catch(Exception) for absent element

response:
## 1) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Bug
Title: Fix call to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` so `UsernameForm` compiles

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47-47

Explanation:
`UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The method added in `UsernamePasswordForm` (lines 160-162) only has the signature `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and no no-arg overload exists. As a result the `services` module will not compile.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) {
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Stop requiring a user before showing conditional passkeys, which breaks normal passkey login

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:113-117
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:137-140

Explanation:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `false` whenever `user == null`.

- Before this change, WebAuthn data was filled in exactly when no user was selected yet, which is the regular first-login case (`context.getUser() == null`).
- After this change, `fillContextForm` is never called for an unidentified user, in either `authenticate()` or `challenge()`.

So conditional UI and the "Sign in with passkey" form disappear from the normal login page. Only re-authentication shows them. That reverses the intent of the change.

The tests in this PR expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial login page (e.g. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` lines 196 and 238). They would fail with this predicate.

The fix is to drop the `user != null` condition so the user does not gate the check. The intent is to show passkeys both on the initial page and during re-authentication.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) {
    return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Ensure the passkey used during re-authentication belongs to the already-identified user

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-67
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47-47

Explanation:
During re-authentication (`prompt=login`), the context user is already set. However:

- `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` now always returns `false` for conditional UI.
- `isUserIdentified` stays `false` and `allowCredentials` is not restricted.

This means any discoverable passkey can be presented. If `WebAuthnAuthenticator.action` (not visible in this diff) resolves the user from the `userHandle` without comparing it to the existing `context.getUser()`, a different user's passkey could complete the "re-authentication" and switch the session user.

Please verify that `action()` rejects a credential whose user differs from the pre-set user. If it does not, add that check. Severity is lowered because this depends on code outside the diff.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// in WebAuthnAuthenticator.action, after resolving user from userHandle
if (context.getUser() != null && !context.getUser().getId().equals(resolvedUser.getId())) {
    context.getEvent().error(Errors.DIFFERENT_USER_AUTHENTICATED);
    // fail / challenge with error
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Add `@Override` on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` override

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-67

Explanation:
This method overrides a superclass hook but is not annotated. If the base signature changes, the override would silently stop applying. Here that would re-enable showing authenticators in conditional UI.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
@Override
protected boolean shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext context) {
    return false;
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Avoid util-to-browser package dependency by moving the constant

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58-58
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/util/AuthenticatorUtils.java:35-35

Explanation:
The constant `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` was widened from `protected` to `public` only so that `AuthenticatorUtils` can import it. This creates a dependency from the generic `util` package back onto a concrete `browser` authenticator class. It also expands public API surface.

Define the constant in `AuthenticatorUtils` (or a constants class) and reference it from the authenticator instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// AuthenticatorUtils
public static final String USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH = "USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH";
// AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator
protected static final String USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH = AuthenticatorUtils.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Use `assertThrows` instead of try/fail/catch(Exception) for absent element

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:291-296
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:312-317

Explanation:
The current pattern catches any `Exception` and treats it as "expected". As a result, unrelated failures (e.g. a stale element or a WebDriver error) pass silently. The `assertThat(..., nullValue())` inside the try block is also dead logic, because `findElement` never returns null.

The same file already uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` elsewhere, which is clearer and stricter.

The comment at line 304 also says passkeys are hidden "as this user does not have passkey". The actual reason is that passkeys are disabled for the realm, so the comment is misleading.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class,
        () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")));
~~~
